qa.q: What are the 5 consistency levels in Azure Cosmos DB and which is default?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Strong, Bounded Staleness, Session (default), Consistent Prefix, and Eventual. Session consistency provides monotonic reads and writes within a client session at low latency and standard RU cost.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** EF Core builds an Expression Tree, translates it via the relational SQL provider into a parameterized T-SQL query, and materializes entities into the DbContext Change Tracker. N+1 queries occur when navigating un-included navigation properties in a loop.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Executing queries without AsNoTracking() in read-only APIs forces EF Core to keep snapshot copies of all returned entities in memory, causing high RAM usage and CPU tracking overhead.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** AsNoTracking() speeds up read queries by 20-30% and reduces memory footprint, but disables identity resolution and automatic change tracking for updates.

qa.q: Why is Managed Identity superior to storing Azure Service Principal secrets in App Settings?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Managed Identity eliminates credential management entirely: Azure automatically creates and rotates secrets under the hood, binding identity to the Azure resource lifespan.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Boxing allocates a System.Object header (16 bytes on x64) on the managed heap and copies the value type bytes into it. Span<T> is a ref struct allocated strictly on the execution stack, providing contiguous memory access without heap allocation or array copying.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Boxing inside a high-throughput loop generates thousands of ephemeral Gen 0 objects, triggering frequent GC pauses and thread pool delays. Fix: use generic collection interfaces (IList<T>) and Span<T>/Memory<T> for byte slicing.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Span<T> provides zero-allocation performance, but ref struct rules forbid storing it on the heap, as class fields, or across async await points (where Memory<T> must be used).
